18.description: Saskatoon is developing a multi-year accessibility plan based on community feedback to identify and remove barriers for residents. The plan outlines city actions to improve infrastructure, services, and address biases.

chips.text: Committee member suggests direct consultation with deaf-blind community for better solutions.
Feedback on the plan has been largely positive.
Plan aims to help people with disabilities and older adults live independently.
City will update sidewalk bylaws and improve snow removal methods.

11.description: The Chair updated council on efforts to improve construction site accessibility and safety, including new ramp styles and considerations for the deafblind community.

chips.text: Signals and awareness efforts are being developed for the deafblind community.
Administration will provide an update on construction accessibility in January.

17.description: Saskatoon faces accessibility challenges for blind and deafblind residents, including low audible pedestrian signals, inaccessible e-scooter reporting, and transit platform deficiencies.

chips.text: Staff confirmed audible signals adjust volume automatically to ambient noise.
Staff asked which e-scooter company had inaccessible reporting.
Garbage and recycling bins are indistinguishable by touch for blind users.
Traffic signal shop will review the location and adjust volume if needed.
